incidente.resumo: On 28 June 2018 an unknown entity gained the password of a Gentoo GitHub organization administrator, removed all developers' access and pushed malicious commits (including rm -rf payloads) to the gentoo, musl and systemd repositories on GitHub; GitHub was unavailable for Gentoo use for approximately 5 days. GitHub froze the organization, Gentoo removed the compromised account's access, force-pushed the repositories back to their known-good state, and GitHub later unlocked the organization.

descricao.texto: Removing all developers caused everyone to get emailed (earliest removal email at 20:26 UTC); at 20:29 the first person noticed something was going on with the GitHub organization, and at 20:36 it was first reported to Infra.
trechos: The attack was loud; removing all developers caused everyone to get emailed.
20:26 Earliest email timestamp of someone being removed from the organization.
20:29 First person notices that something is going on with the GitHub organization
20:36 First report to Infra that something is going on with the GitHub organization.

gatilho.texto: At 20:19 UTC on 2018-06-28, after trying a bad password on the account, the attacker gained administrative access to the Gentoo GitHub organization, and at 20:25 started removing valid users.
trechos: 20:19 Attacker tries a bad password on the account.
20:19 Attacker successfully gains administrative access
20:25 Attacker starts removing valid users

descricao.texto: The attacker gained access to the password of an organization administrator; the evidence collected suggests a password scheme where disclosure on one site made it easy to guess passwords for unrelated webpages.
trechos: The attacker gained access to a password of an organization administrator.
Evidence collected suggests a password scheme where disclosure on one site made it easy to guess passwords for unrelated webpages.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: GitHub did not block access to the repositories via git, so the malicious commits were externally accessible until Gentoo force-pushed over them.
trechos: GitHub failed to block access to the repositories via git, resulting in the malicious commits being externally accessible.
Gentoo had to force-push over them as soon as this was discovered that.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Credential revocation procedures were incomplete; during the access revocation, some hosts were missed.
trechos: Credential revocation procedures were incomplete.
Note: During the access revocation, some hosts were missed.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: There was no backup copy of the Gentoo GitHub Organization detail.
trechos: We did not have a backup copy of the Gentoo GitHub Organization detail.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The systemd repository is not mirrored from Gentoo infrastructure but stored directly on GitHub.
trechos: The systemd repo is not mirrored from Gentoo, but is stored directly on GitHub.

passos.texto: Gentoo escalated to GitHub support (abuse reports from 20:49, formal ticket at 21:05), and at 21:28 GitHub support responded and froze the Gentoo GitHub organization.
trechos: Gentoo Developers & Infrastructure escalated to GitHub support and the Gentoo Organization was frozen by GitHub staff.
20:49 First abuse report to GitHub support
21:05 Infra's formal ticket to GitHub Support
21:28 GitHub support responds; Gentoo GitHub org frozen.

passos.texto: At 22:45 GitHub locked the suspected entry point; at 23:40 Gentoo determined which account was the entry point and preemptively removed all access for that account from primary Gentoo properties (git repos, bugs, email, etc.).
trechos: 22:45 GitHub locks suspected entry point
23:40 Gentoo determines which account was the entry point. Gentoo Infra preemptively removes all access for that account from primary Gentoo properties (git repos, bugs, email, etc.)

passos.texto: At Gentoo's request, GitHub re-hid the organization at 00:25 on 2018-06-29 while Gentoo carried out repairs; Gentoo Infra restored the billing email at 05:27.
trechos: 00:05 Gentoo emails GitHub, requesting the org be hidden again while Gentoo affects repairs. Of particular concern are the PRs and how we can audit them.
00:25 GitHub responds saying they have re-hidden the org, and will wait for confirmation before un-hiding it again, but are concerned about proper operation for organization members
05:27 Gentoo Infra restores billing email.

passos.texto: Between 06:57 and 06:59 on 2018-06-29, Gentoo Infra force-pushed gentoo/systemd, gentoo/gentoo and gentoo/musl back to their last legitimate commits to restore state.
trechos: 06:57 Gentoo Infra does force-push on *gentoo/systemd* to restore state. c46d8bbf->bf0e0a4d.
06:58 Gentoo Infra does force-push on *gentoo/gentoo* to restore state. e6db0eb4->73b72409.
06:59 Gentoo Infra does force-push on *gentoo/musl* to restore state. e6db0eb4->60461ca1.

passos.texto: At 13:05 on 2018-06-29 GitHub unlocked the compromised account and reset its password.
trechos: 13:05 GitHub unlocks the compromised account and resets the password.

passos.texto: At 11:46 on 2018-07-03, GitHub unlocked the Gentoo GitHub Organization, making it publicly visible again.
trechos: 11:46 GitHub responds and unlocks the Gentoo GitHub Organization, making it publicly visible once again,

Approximately 5 days of GitHub being unavailable for Gentoo use.

observacoes: Duration uses the stated approximately 5 days; the timeline runs from administrative access at 20:19 UTC on 2018-06-28 to the organization being unlocked at 11:46 UTC on 2018-07-03. Malicious content was available in initial clones of gentoo/gentoo, gentoo/musl and gentoo/systemd between about 20:38 on 2018-06-28 and 06:59 on 2018-06-29. The Gentoo-hosted master repositories were not affected. Logs indicate GitHub accounts were probed between 2018-04-08 and 2018-06-27. All past pull requests were apparently disconnected from their commits and closed. The text says the rm -rf payloads were unlikely to be executed by end users due to technical guards. Gentoo recommends that anyone who cloned gentoo/gentoo, gentoo/musl or gentoo/systemd during the listed intervals recreate the clone from a new clone (remediation, not prevention).
